name: TU Delft V3 kite, 4 mm Dyneema tether of the 20 kW pumping system (OF-0009 case C2)

bridle.note: The V3 CAD frame of the aircraft case has its origin about 11 m below the wing, at the bridle/KCU; the tether is attached there (pivot at the origin, a 0.5 m leg towards the last tether node, which is the swing model of tether/bridle.py).

sources.length_m: traction phase of the two test flights, 234-385 m and 390-720 m (van der Vlugt et al. 2019, Renewable Energy 131:83-99, Table 1); 300 m chosen inside the first range
sources.outer_diameter_m: 4 mm (van der Vlugt et al. 2019, Table 1)
sources.linear_density_kg_m: tether density 724 kg/m3 (van der Vlugt et al. 2019, Table 1) times the section area of a 4 mm circle: 0.0091 kg/m
sources.section_drag_coeff: 1.1, cylinder in cross flow at Re 2.7e3-8.2e3 (van der Vlugt et al. 2019, Section 3.4)
sources.tensile_stiffness_N: unit spring constant k0 = 614600 N of the 4 mm main tether (Fechner, van der Vlugt, Schreuder, Schmehl 2015, Renewable Energy 83:705-716, Table 2; arXiv 1406.6218)
sources.longitudinal_damping_ratio: Makani default of the line model kept (0.1); Fechner et al. 2015 give a unit damping c0 = 473 N s, not transcribed
sources.num_nodes: 20 nodes, segments of 15 m; the stability bound of the explicit RK4 line step is checked by the driver
sources.declared_strain_for_the_sphere: tether force 3.0-3.1 kN in the traction phase (van der Vlugt et al. 2019, Table 1) over k0: 0.0049, rounded to 0.005
